longQuestions: Shape is the base class at the top; Circle, Rectangle, Triangle and Square are derived from it (hierarchical inheritance). The arrows point from each derived class to the base class.

An object is an instance of a class — a variable of the class type that has its own copy of the data members and can use the member functions. A class is a blueprint; objects are the real entities made from it.

Objects are created by declaring them with the class name: class_name object_name; e.g. Student s1, s2; Members are accessed with the dot (member access) operator: s1.getData(); s1.show(); (only public members can be accessed from outside the class; with a pointer the arrow operator is used: p->show();).

Inheritance is the process of creating a new (derived) class from an existing (base) class; the derived class gets the members of the base class and can add its own, giving code reusability. Example: class Car : public Vehicle { … }; Car inherits speed and start() from Vehicle and adds airConditioner.

Polymorphism means 'many forms' — the same name behaves differently in different situations. Compile-time polymorphism: function overloading (area(int), area(int, int)) and operator overloading. Run-time polymorphism: virtual functions overridden in derived classes, e.g. Shape has virtual void draw(); Circle and Square each define draw() differently, and a Shape* calls the right one at run time.
